title: Pull requests from an agent
bridge: An agent's PR is like a PR you open as a draft and only mark ready when CI is green. Except: the author is a bot, so the PR must name the person who asked in a Requested-by line. And the bot may open drafts and mark its own PR ready, but it can never approve or merge.
intro: p2-5 taught the Octokit calls. This lesson is about the life of an agent's PR. Who opens it, what its title and last line say, and how required checks decide when it leaves draft. Then the one GraphQL call that marks it ready. People are pinged only when the PR is clean.

picture.caption: The harness asks, the broker writes with a one-repo token, and the ready gate pings people only when the PR is clean.

steps.text: asks to open a PR for branch nova/RH-1234; the VM holds no token
pulls.create with draft: true and the Requested-by line last
reads required checks (gh pr checks --required), QA results, judges and findings
all clean: markPullRequestReadyForReview, then request the reviewer team
only now is anyone pinged; one approval from someone who is not Dana

sections.h: The life of an agent PR
p: Nova works on the branch nova/RH-1234 and pushes a checkpoint after each step that passes, with [skip ci] in the message. When the work is done, it asks the broker to open a draft PR. Byte reviews the draft, Nova fixes what Byte finds, and CI runs.

The PR stays a draft until everything is clean. Then the ready gate marks it ready and requests the reviewer team. The Jira ticket goes back to the requester, and Slack gets a post. A person reviews, one other person approves, and a person merges. The agent never does those last three.

callout.text: G4-27: people's attention is the scarcest part of this loop. Pinging them only for clean PRs keeps their trust in Nova.

sections.h: Title, branch and the Requested-by line
p: The title follows fcp's habit: [FE] RH-1234: what changes. The body uses the pr-story headings and keeps ### References with the Jira link, so add-jira-links finds it. The last line is always Requested-by: @<github login>.

That line matters because the PR's author is the bot rhino-ai-agents[bot]. GitHub stops authors approving their own PRs, but here the author is a bot. The independent-approval check (G0-09) reads the line and refuses an approval from that person. A PR without the line fails closed. For a routine, the line names the routine's owner.
sections.because: We build the line in one function because a missing or wrong login silently breaks the approval wall.

notes.text: The same pattern the approval check uses (G0-09). Test the line against it before writing.
The team prefix and the Jira key, like every fcp PR title.
The run's one branch. The broker's git proxy refuses pushes anywhere else.
The requester is known by Jira accountId; GitHub needs the login. people.yaml maps them.
No mapping: fail loudly. A PR with a guessed requester is worse than no PR.
The last line of the body, after the pr-story sections and References.

p: The VM has no GitHub token. The harness asks the broker, and the broker's POST /v1/gh allow-list decides. It may create a draft PR, mark the run's own PR ready, view, diff, read checks and comment on its own PR. It may never merge, approve or change settings.
The broker mints a GitHub App token for one repo and one hour. It has contents and pull_requests write, and checks and actions read. Never workflows, so no agent push can change .github/workflows.
sections.because: We open the PR in the broker because the token never enters the VM, and the broker knows the run's branch.

notes.text: A fresh installation token for this run's repo. It is used here and never returned.
head comes from the run's scope, not from the request, so a run cannot open a PR from another branch.
The body gets the Requested-by line here, in one place.
Always draft. Drafts do not request reviews or notify CODEOWNERS.
Byte's broker pattern: every write and every refused write is audited.
node_id is the PR's GraphQL ID. Keep it: marking ready needs it.

sections.h: Reading checks: only the required ones
p: A PR has many checks, and only the required ones block a merge. gh pr checks <n> --required --json name,bucket lists them. bucket groups each check's state into pass, fail, pending, skipping or cancel, so the code needs no table of conclusions.

The ready gate treats anything but pass and skipping as a blocker, a pending check included. Then it adds the other evidence: QA checks, the scope judge, the PR judge and important findings that are still open. If main fails the same check, Nova links main's failing run and flags it instead of looping.
sections.because: We gate on required checks, not all checks, because only those decide whether a person could merge.

notes.text: Finding states that count as handled. Anything else that is important blocks.
Through the broker: gh with --required and JSON output. One call, every required check.
pass and skipping are fine; fail, pending and cancel block.
Every QA check from the agreed plan must have passed.
Any blocker: stay a draft, ping nobody, and return the reasons.
Clean: leave draft. In the broker this is the GraphQL call below.
Request the reviewer team by area: frontend-guild for frontend/**, backend-guild for cloud/** and client/**.

sections.h: Marking ready is a GraphQL call
p: The REST endpoint that updates a PR cannot take it out of draft. GitHub's GraphQL API has the mutation markPullRequestReadyForReview, and gh pr ready uses it. It takes the PR's node_id, which pulls.create returned.
The broker checks first that the PR belongs to this run. A run can mark only its own PR ready, never another one.
sections.because: We check the PR's owner first, so 'mark ready' can never ping people about someone else's PR.

notes.text: A GraphQL mutation with one variable, the PR's node ID.
We ask for isDraft back, to confirm the change happened.
The scope wall: only the run's own PR (G3-07).
octokit.graphql sends the query with variables. Errors throw like REST errors.
false isDraft means ready. Then the workflow sets Nova state to PR open and assigns Jira back.

p: Exactly one approval, from a person who is not the requester, is a GitHub wall. The ruleset requires it and G0-09's check enforces who. The rhino-ai-agents App has no permission to merge and no bypass. The agent also never edits the checks it is judged by: locked checks block that (G0-18).
After ready, people's review comments go back into Nova's fix-or-answer loop. If nobody reviews for 2 days, Nova reminds once (G3-38).

callout.text: The requester never approves their own agent's PR, and exactly one approval is needed. Agents never merge.

lab.title: Read a draft PR the way the ready gate does
youNeed: Your scratch repo actions-lab from p2 (with a workflow that runs on pull_request)

worked.do: cd ~/actions-lab && git switch -c nova/LAB-1 && echo lab >> README.md && git commit -am 'LAB-1: a lab change' && git push -u origin nova/LAB-1

gh pr create --draft --title '[FE] LAB-1: a lab change' --body $'### References
- LAB-1

Requested-by: @<your login>'
GITHUB_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) npx tsx pr-lab.ts <n> while the workflow still runs
worked.see:
#<n> draft=true node_id=PR_kwDO... requested-by=<your login>
stays draft: <job name> is pending

worked.do: Wait for the run to finish (gh pr checks <n> --watch), then run pr-lab.ts again
Mark it ready yourself: gh pr ready <n>. Run pr-lab.ts again.
Put it back: gh pr ready <n> --undo

lab.faded: Edit the PR body on GitHub and delete the Requested-by line. Left to you: predict pr-lab.ts's output, run it, and say which wall that output protects.
lab.alone: Write withRequestedBy for the lab: a small people.json mapping a fake Jira accountId to your GitHub login. It must throw for an unknown accountId and put the line last. Test both cases with node:test, then print the body you would send.
lab.done: Your read-only script found the Requested-by line, kept a pending PR as a draft, and named the node_id it would mark ready.

words.plain: A PR opened with draft: true; it requests no reviews and notifies nobody.
The last line of an agent PR body, Requested-by: @login; that person can never approve it.
A check the ruleset demands before merge; the ready gate reads only these.
gh pr checks' simple state per check: pass, fail, pending, skipping or cancel.
A PR's GraphQL ID, returned by pulls.create; GraphQL mutations need it.
G4-27's activity that marks a PR ready only when checks, QA, judges and findings are clean.

tickets.why: readyGate reads required checks and evidence, and only then marks ready and requests reviewers.
The PR body uses the pr-story headings, keeps ### References, and always ends with Requested-by.
The independent-approval check reads the Requested-by line and fails closed without it.
The broker's POST /v1/gh allow-list opens drafts and marks only the run's own PR ready, with a one-repo token.

remember: Agents open drafts through the broker, end the body with Requested-by, and leave draft only when every required check is clean.
